rationale: All four of my round-2 items are ADDRESSED at 9ac301ee, each re-derived. (1) OQ-1(c) tagging: AC-6 now splits the arm-independent retry-convergence assertion from the (c)-only diff-pathspec assertion with the correct rationale (under (a)/(b) no delta is ever left past the reviewed SHA), AC-7 scopes leg (i) as arm-independent and legs (ii)-(iv) as (c)-only, and OQ-1's closing sentence is reconciled to say exactly that ('convergence ACs hold under any ... exemption-shape legs exist under (c) only and are tagged so in place') — the contradiction I flagged is gone, resolved more cleanly than my ask (tagging (ii)/(iv) as (c)-only rather than leaving them vacuously true is the better shape). (2) Release row: the tail-less two-surface carve-out is stated in R1.3 the same way the plan-approve carve-out is, and the fix went beyond my ask with a genuine discovery — release's step-6.5 sync calls the stored-trusting phase.DerivePhase and re-syncs stored 'implement' on the all-open state it just created; I verified release.go:315-318 does exactly that (DerivePhase → deps.syncPhase when releasing the active bead), making release a real second deterministic route into the #248 warning window, now carried consistently through R3.1/R3.2/AC-5(i)-(ii). (3) AC-14: the count-sentinel arm is dropped and anti-drift is mechanized as total classification over the registered cobra command tree (every command either in the mutating row set or a rationale-carrying non-mutating allowlist) — this actually delivers the red-on-add promise. (4) AC-4: rewritten as two mutually exclusive branches with the always-indeterminate degenerate implementation explicitly failing the success branch. The consistency scan over the other changed surfaces also holds up: R6.7/AC-15's silent-global-fallback claim is grounded (I verified next.go:166-171's epicErr→QueryReady() fallback, matching the runEmitOnly copy I verified in round 2) and AC-15 is runnable/red-on-revert via the bd seams; the R3.3 flock mechanism rests on a real idiom (internal/journal's withReportsLock/acquireFileLock — whose own doc comment confirms two same-process descriptors contend, validating AC-5(v)'s contending-goroutine test design); the G1 repro line is now self-consistent via the absolute-path invocation. Three MINOR residuals remain (below); the only substantive one is a Scope-list lag behind R3.3's new lock-writer enumeration, mechanical to fix and unambiguous in intent, so it does not warrant a fourth blocked round.
concrete_changes_required: Sync the In Scope list with R3.3's lock-writer enumeration: R3.3 now mandates the stored-phase write lock be held by plan approve's write (plan.go:455) and the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write UNCONDITIONALLY, but In Scope still lists internal/approve/plan.go as touched 'only if OQ-3 resolves against the stored-implement write', and the impl approve/adopt write site (cmd/mindspec/impl.go or wherever the terminal write lives) appears nowhere in In Scope. Amend the plan.go entry ('...or for the R3.3 lock acquisition') and add the impl-approve write site, so a plan implementing R3.3 does not violate the spec's own Scope.

AC-2's carve-out parenthetical names only '(the plan-approve row under OQ-3 option 2)' and its fixture-alternative branch describes only the stored/derived-pair shape; the release row now carries a documented tail-less TWO-SURFACE carve-out as well. Extend the parenthetical and the alternative branch (e.g. '...or asserts only the row's documented surface subset for a tail-less row') so the release row's fixture is unambiguously AC-2-conformant.

Plan-stage chartering note (no spec text change strictly required, but one sentence would close it): if the plan takes R1.3's release-sync redesign leg (the sanctioned internal caller performing a guard-routed backward write), no AC currently pins the sanction boundary — that the operator repair-phase path still refuses backward without force, and that only the enumerated internal caller may take the guard-routed move. Either add the one-sentence AC obligation now or ensure the plan's panel inherits it explicitly.

findings.title: Round-2 ask classification: all 4 ADDRESSED (re-derived against the tree)
findings.detail: Ask 1 (AC-7(iii)/AC-6 OQ-1(c) tagging): ADDRESSED — AC-6 splits the arm-independent retry assertion from the (c)-only pathspec assertion; AC-7 tags legs (ii)-(iv) as (c)-only with leg (i) arm-independent; OQ-1's 'hold under any arm' sentence is reconciled to name exactly which legs are arm-independent. The fix's choice to tag (ii)/(iv) as (c)-only (rather than my weaker leave-them-vacuous framing) is the better resolution. Ask 2 (release-row tail-less carve-out): ADDRESSED and exceeded — beyond the tail-less two-surface carve-out, the fix documents that release's step-6.5 sync is stored-trusting under BOTH OQ-3 options; verified: cmd/mindspec/release.go:315-318 calls phase.DerivePhase (the stored-trusting path whose warning emission I verified at derive.go:175-193 in round 1) and syncs its result when the released bead was active, so the second-fixture-route claim in R3.1 and the stored-vs-derived split in the row are both grounded. Ask 3 (AC-14 anti-drift): ADDRESSED — count-sentinel arm dropped with my rationale quoted; the replacement (total classification over the registered cobra command tree, red on any unclassified new command and red on mutating-without-row) is mechanized and falsifiable. Ask 4 (AC-4 branch scoping): ADDRESSED — two mutually exclusive branches, each asserted only in its driving case, with the always-indeterminate implementation named as failing the success branch.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: In Scope lags R3.3's rewritten lock-writer enumeration
findings.detail: The round-2 G6 rewrite makes R3.3's advisory lock mandatory for 'every other mindspec_phase writer', enumerated as plan approve's plan.go:455 write, complete's step-6.5 sync, release's step-6.5 sync, and the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write. But In Scope still carries the pre-existing condition 'internal/approve/plan.go (only if OQ-3 resolves against the stored-implement write)' — false now, since the lock wraps that write under every OQ-3 outcome — and lists no impl-approve/adopt write site at all (cmd/mindspec/release.go was added this round; impl.go was not). The requirement text is unambiguous, so this is a scope-list precision defect rather than a design hole, but Scope is what charters the beads; one line each closes it.

findings.title: AC-2 not updated for the release row's two-surface carve-out
findings.detail: AC-2's alternative branch covers 'a row carrying a documented carve-out' but describes only the stored/derived-pair shape and names only the plan-approve row as its example; its main clause still lists three surfaces including the instruct tail. The release row's tail-less carve-out (R1.3 (i), fixture asserts state show + derivation only) is documented in R1.3 and fits the intent chain, but a literal reading of AC-2 would demand a tail assertion for a verb R2.1 records as tail-less. Extend AC-2's example list and alternative branch to cover surface-subset carve-outs.

findings.title: Release-sync redesign leg, if taken, has no AC pinning the internal-caller sanction boundary
findings.detail: R1.3's redesign leg would let release's sync perform a legitimate backward write 'routed through R3.3's guard machinery as its sanctioned internal caller (never the operator force flag)'. AC-5(ii)/(iii) pin the operator path (refusal, force+reason); nothing pins that the sanctioned internal route stays confined to the enumerated caller or that taking the leg leaves the operator refusal intact. The leg is explicitly a plan-time decision alongside OQ-3, so this can be chartered to the plan's panel — but it should be inherited explicitly, not rediscovered.

findings.title: New round-3 claims spot-verified (no defects found)
findings.detail: Verified rather than inherited: release.go:315-318 stored-trusting sync (grounds the second fixture route and the release-row stored-vs-derived split); internal/journal withReportsLock/acquireFileLock (lock.go, lock_unix.go:22, lock_windows.go:25) — the idiom R3.3's mechanism cites exists, and its doc comment confirms flock contends across two open descriptors within one process, which is what makes AC-5(v)'s contending-goroutine leg testable in-process; next.go:166-171's epicErr→QueryReady() silent global fallback (grounds R6.7's citation and AC-15(iii)'s red-on-revert); the G1 validation-proof line now resolves mindspec to an absolute path before PATH narrows, making the repro self-consistent. AC-11's new termsafe rendering leg and AC-5(iii)'s reason-in-output leg are both runnable and red-on-revert as written.
